newsitem.title: JAPAN: Administrative steps vs DKB depend on probe-source.
newsitem.headline: Administrative steps vs DKB depend on probe-source.

text.p: Administrative penalties against scandal-tainted Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) will be decided depending on what prosecutors discover in their investigations into the bank's affairs, a Japanese financial source said on Friday.
Earlier on Friday the Finance Ministry filed a complaint against DKB and four former officials of the bank alleging violations of Japan's Banking Law.
The source, who did not want to be identified, said the ministry understood that the bank itself had committed violations of the Banking Law, not only the four former officials.

Another source, who also did not want to be identified, said the four former DKB officials were former DKB vice president Tsuneo Uchida, former managing directors Yasuyuki Terasawa and Hiroshi Inozume, and former executive Michiyoshi Kusajima.
The complaints accuse DKB of concealing information about problem loans to a corporate racketeer, Ryuichi Koike, when the ministry carried out an inspection in October 1994, he said.
"The ministry filed complaints against DKB as the bank's misdeeds were against ministry inspections aimed at maintaining the soundness of banks," he said.
MOF received an in-house investigation report from DKB earlier on Friday and this had led to the complaint to prosecutors, the first financial source said.
